hypotheses.title: Single global mutex in semtypes BDD key interner serialises concurrent type resolution
hypotheses.issue: semtypes/canonical_key.go internBddNodeKey interns every new BDD node key (bddNodeKey{atom,left,middle,right}) into one process-wide map bddKeyInterner.keys guarded by a single sync.Mutex. It runs on every BDD node construction (bdd_node_simple.go / bdd_node_impl.go, reached from bddNodeCreate, Diff, bddDiff, IsSubtype ...). Stage 5 (semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go ResolvePrivateNodes) resolves each function body in its own goroutine and stages 5-9 also run concurrently per module, so every semtype operation in every goroutine serialises on this one lock. Hot callers: lambda typing (resolveInferredLambdaFunctionExpr, IsSubtype on function types), opaque map() monomorphization (semantics/internal/opaque/registry.go buildFunctionDefinitions), functionPathIsEmpty. Profile on the reproducer: internBddNodeKey ~17% of CPU samples, ~96% of total mutex contention, ~79% of Mutex.Lock block delay; process CPU utilisation only ~280% on 4 cores. Ids only need to be unique per distinct key and assigned children-before-parents (a child is always interned before its parent's key is built), so a single global lock is not required. The map is also never cleared (grows for the process lifetime; ~6% of allocated bytes from map growth on corpus/bench/10-bench/expressions-v.bal) - not addressed by the prototype.

reproducer.command: python3 gen_multimodule.py 8 600 bddpkg && go build -o /tmp/perfhunt/bal ./cli/cmd && /usr/bin/time -v /tmp/perfhunt/bal run --stats bddpkg   # also: ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> bddpkg

hypotheses.baseline: main @ BASE, 4 cores: wall 4.8-5.3 s (benchmark mean 5238 ms), max RSS 1.3-1.6 GB, --stats Analysis summed over modules 20.9-28.6 s of Total 23.5-32.3 s; CPU ~280%. Program prints 9688.

improvement.summary: Wall time -14.66% (5238 ms -> 4470 ms, 3.81 sigma); summed Analysis stage time ~-37% (21-28 s -> 14-15 s); single-file variant ~-10% wall; peak RSS unchanged within noise (memory run unreliable, -6.5%).

hypotheses.fix_approach: Replace the single mutex+map with 64 shards (each a mutex + map[bddNodeKey]bddKey, padded to a cache line), chosen by a cheap multiply-xor hash of the key fields; allocate new ids from a global atomic.Int64 counter. A key always maps to the same shard and lookup+insert happen under that shard's lock, so each distinct key gets exactly one id; the atomic counter keeps ids unique and monotonic, so children still get smaller ids than parents. Callers are unchanged. make test and make test-race pass. Pitfalls/follow-ups: the interner still never shrinks (unbounded growth across a long-lived process); id order across shards is no longer globally serialised but nothing relies on that beyond uniqueness/child-before-parent. Remaining CPU headroom (~280% of 400%) suggests other serial sections (e.g. per-function semtypes.ContextFrom allocation, env.typeAtom returning an escaping copy) could be looked at next.

notes: Exploration also noted (not pursued): fresh semtypes context per function body/lambda (~6% alloc bytes), env.typeAtom heap-escaping copy (~3% alloc bytes), 09-bench/huge-project-v ~9 GB RSS and too noisy to measure.
